layers.name: Areas of Special Scientific Interest (ASSI)
layers.description: Areas of Special Scientific Interest provide statutory protection under the Nature Conservation and Amenity Lands (NI) Order 1985 for the best examples of NI's flora, fauna, geological or physiographical features. layers.name: Landscape Character Areas (LCA)

layers.name: National Nature Reserves (NNR)
layers.description: Statutory nature reserves declared under the Nature Conservation and Amenity Lands (NI) Order 1985 for areas of importance for flora, fauna, geological or other special features. layers.name: Ramsar Wetland Sites

layers.name: Special Areas of Conservation (SAC)

layers.name: Special Protection Areas (SPA)

layers.name: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1971
layers.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1971-04-15, assembled from Connacht (= 1957 boundaries), Leinster 1971, Munster 1971, Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1977. In 1977, due to the expansion of Drogheda, part of the DED of St. Mary’s was ceded to County Louth by County Meath. Details on this can be found in the Local Government Provisional Order Confirmation Act, 1976. Also relevant is the renaming of An Uaimh to Navan on 25/06/1971, as its corresponding DEDs were renamed by 1971 Census Reports Volume 1 (published July 1972).

layers.name: Tellus Electromagnetic — 14 kHz Apparent Conductivity
layers.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 14 kHz — shallower depth (~10–30 m) than the 3 kHz channel, more sensitive to surface and near-surface conductors. Useful for soil moisture, near-surface alteration, and thin clay layers. Viridis colormap, -2σ to +4σ stretch.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-em-14khz/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Electromagnetic — 3 kHz Apparent Conductivity
layers.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 3 kHz from the Tellus airborne EM survey — penetrates ~50–150 m, mapping conductive saline groundwater, clay-rich soils, mineralised zones, and pollution plumes. Viridis colormap (low = purple, high = yellow), -2σ to +4σ stretch.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-em-3khz/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Airborne Survey — Flight Lines
layers.description: The actual flight-line pattern flown by the Tellus airborne geophysical survey (2005–2008) — 2 210 individual flight lines at ~250 m spacing across all of Northern Ireland, derived from the raw radiometric sample positions. Toggle on alongside any of the gridded magnetic / electromagnetic / radiometric layers to see where the survey actually sampled the ground; anomalies on the gridded products are most reliable inside dense flight coverage and progressively less reliable on the edges and in gaps. Single inert MultiLineString — non-interactive (no per-line popup, hover, or click) so it doesn't compete with the per-feature data layers underneath.
layers.notes: Generated from render/source-cache/vector-intake/tellus-flight-tracks.fgb with GDAL MVT output.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — Reduction-to-Pole (RTP)
layers.description: TMI corrected by reduction-to-pole, which compensates for the dipolar shape of magnetic anomalies caused by NI's inclined magnetic field. RTP places the peak directly above the source body, simplifying interpretation. ±3σ rainbow ramp.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-mag-rtp/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — RTP Tilt Derivative
layers.description: Tilt derivative of the RTP magnetic field — an edge-detection filter that highlights the boundaries of magnetic source bodies regardless of their amplitude. Excellent for tracing dykes, faults, and contacts. ±3σ rainbow ramp.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-mag-rtp-tilt/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Magnetic — Total Magnetic Intensity (residual)
layers.description: Residual total magnetic intensity (TMI) from the GSNI Tellus airborne survey — variations in the Earth's magnetic field caused by buried magnetic minerals (chiefly magnetite). High-magnetic anomalies trace mafic/ultramafic intrusions, basaltic flows, and iron-bearing sedimentary basins; magnetic lows mark sedimentary basins and demagnetised alteration zones. 35m grid spacing, ±3σ rainbow ramp.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-mag-tmi/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Potassium (K %)
layers.description: Surface potassium concentration from natural gamma-ray emissions. Highlights granites and other felsic intrusions (potassium-rich), alkaline volcanics, and certain sedimentary horizons. Inferno colormap (dark = low, bright = high), ±2-3σ stretch.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-k/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — K/Th/U Ternary RGB
layers.description: The iconic radiometric ternary composite — K mapped to red, Th to green, U to blue. Reds = potassic (granite, certain volcanics); greens = thorium-rich (resistate sediments, heavy minerals); blues = uranium-rich (organic shales, mineralisation); whites/pale = high in all three; blacks = low overall. The most interpretively powerful single radiometric view. Each band stretched independently to mean ± 2σ.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-ternary/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Thorium-Equivalent (eTh ppm)
layers.description: Thorium-equivalent concentration from the 2.61 MeV thallium-208 daughter peak. Often correlates with heavy minerals (monazite, zircon) in placer deposits and resistate sediments. Rainbow colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-th/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Total Counts (gamma)
layers.description: Total gamma-ray count rate — a summed proxy for combined K, U, Th, and other radionuclide activity. Useful for identifying overall radiometric "hot" zones before decomposing into individual channels. Inferno colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/geology/tellus-rad-total/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.

layers.name: Tellus Radiometric — Uranium-Equivalent (eU ppm)
layers.description: Uranium-equivalent concentration from the 1.76 MeV bismuth-214 daughter peak. Highlights uranium-bearing granites, organic-rich shales, phosphatic horizons, and mineralised zones. Viridis colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

layers.name: Agricultural Critical Risk Areas (DAERA)
layers.description: DAERA classification of land parcels by their relative risk of contributing diffuse agricultural pollution to receiving waters. Each parcel is scored 0–1 (`riskscore2`) by combining slope, hydrological connectivity, soil characteristics, rainfall, river-buffer proximity and land-use rules. Companion to the Network Contribution datasets — the polygon equivalent of the per-river-basin SciMAP score.
layers.notes: Generated from render/source-cache/vector-intake/wq-agricultural-critical-risk.fgb with GDAL MVT output.

layers.name: DAERA Network Contribution — SciMAP modelled pollution scores by river basin (26 catchments)
layers.description: Per-river-basin pollution-contribution scores from the SciMAP hydrological model (CEH Land Cover 2007 + Met Office rainfall + 5 m DTM), rasterised at 25 m and rendered as a Web Mercator tile pyramid coloured on inferno (low → high contribution). Raw GRIDCODE values of 58–100 stretch the inferno ramp from dark purple to pale yellow. Each parcel of land is scored for how much sediment / nutrient pollution its upstream catchment contributes to receiving waters. 26 catchment datasets were rasterised individually, mosaicked, and re-projected; per-catchment download links remain in sourceDownloads for the raw vector data.
layers.notes: Raster XYZ tile layer using metadata bounds and tile template https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/water-quality/network-contribution-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png.
keywords: DAERA Network Contribution — SciMAP modelled pollution scores by river basin (26 catchments)
